The core 3D printing supplies attract 18% GST — this covers 3D printers (HSN 8443), printing services (SAC 998920), and filament (HSN 3916). One notable exception: nozzles and print-heads sold separately fall under a classification within heading 8443 that attracts 28% GST . Always match the rate to what is actually being invoiced.

Yes. They are fundamentally different supplies. 3D printing services use SAC 998920 (a services code for moulding, pressing, extruding and similar plastic manufacturing services). 3D printer filament is a physical good and uses HSN 3916 (plastic monofilament and profile shapes with cross-section greater than 1 mm). Both are taxed at 18%, but the codes are distinct and must be used correctly on the invoice.
